questions.stem: Data Literacy is described as the key for what?
options: All data initiatives
Only machine learning projects
Only financial reporting
Only database administration
Only executive dashboards
questions.explanation: Data Literacy is described as the key for all Data Initiatives.

questions.stem: In previous eras, what was the role of a Business Analyst in relation to a Business Intelligence developer?
options: The BA built the dashboards while the BI developer talked to the business
The BA managed the database while the BI developer wrote KPIs
The BA and BI developer had identical responsibilities
The BA talked to the business, created KPIs and passed them to the BI developer to build reports and dashboards
The BA reviewed the BI developer's code for errors
questions.explanation: In previous eras, the BA talked to the business, created the KPIs and passed them to the BI developer to create reports and dashboards.

questions.stem: According to I Am Datapedia!, what share of Business Intelligence developers in the previous era would not know what a report or dashboard was for?
questions.explanation: The author states that 90% of BI developers would not know what a report or dashboard was for, nor the impact of good and bad reports.

questions.stem: What is the difference between Analysis and Analytics?
options: Analysis is automated while Analytics is manual
Analysis is done on unstructured data while Analytics is done on structured data
Analysis is a tool while Analytics is a job title
Analysis predicts the future while Analytics describes the past
Analysis is about finding the Whys and Whats, whereas Analytics is about finding the Hows
questions.explanation: The difference is simple but tricky: Analysis finds the Whys and Whats from a dataset, whereas Analytics finds the Hows.

questions.stem: How does I Am Datapedia! summarise what Analysis and Analytics each do within a dataset?
options: Analysis stores data and Analytics deletes data
Analysis builds tables and Analytics builds charts
Analysis searches for questions and Analytics proposes answers
Analysis proposes answers and Analytics searches for questions
Analysis and Analytics both only describe the data
questions.explanation: In other words, in datasets Analysis searches for questions and Analytics proposes answers.

questions.stem: What is the current era called, in contrast with the previous era of Analysis?
options: The Analytics era
The Reporting era
The Spreadsheet era
The Storage era
The Dashboard era
questions.explanation: Time has changed and we have entered the Analytics era, as compared to the previous era of Analysis.

questions.stem: When Data Literacy says everyone must understand data and its value, who does everyone include?
options: Only senior executives
Only business analysts
Only data scientists
Everyone from the ETL developer through to the BI developer
Only external consultants
questions.explanation: Everyone means everyone, from the ETL developer till the BI developer; one cannot create something one does not understand.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the questions a data literate person should be able to answer, according to I Am Datapedia!?
options: Where the data comes from and where it will go
Which programming language was used to store the data
Who needs the report and what its purpose is
Which KPIs are served and what value it can generate
What the impact on organisational revenue will be
questions.explanation: The author's data literacy questions cover reading data, its source and destination, who needs it, its purpose, value, KPIs and revenue impact; the storage language is not among them.

questions.stem: In the era before data became a driving force, where did most decision making happen?
options: In machine learning models
In real-time dashboards
In data science notebooks
In NoSQL databases
In reports extracted into Excel
questions.explanation: In that era reports and dashboards were good to have, and most decision making happened in reports extracted into Excel.

questions.stem: According to Data Literacy, what must someone who is creating a report or dashboard do?
options: Obtain a certification first
Use only approved colours
Understand the report or dashboard they are creating
Build it in Excel before any other tool
Ask a data scientist to sign it off
questions.explanation: One cannot create something one does not understand, so anyone creating a report or dashboard must understand it.
